methodologyNotes: Roster covers fourteen torque wrenches spanning 3/8 in. and 1/2 in. drive click, digital/electronic, micrometer-adjustable, and beam-type mechanisms from TEKTON, GearWrench, Precision Instruments, CDI (Snap-on Industrial Brands), ACDelco, Snap-on, Craftsman, Neiko, Park Tool, Lexivon, EPAuto, ARES, Husky, and ICON (Harbor Freight), verified 2026-08-09 against manufacturer/official-brand pages where reachable (tekton.com, gearwrench.com, torqwrench.com, parktool.com, lexivon.com, neikotools.com, craftsman.com, arestool.com, harborfreight.com) and corroborated by authorized-dealer or major-retailer listings (Home Depot, Walmart, Zoro, PartsSource, Amazon) where the manufacturer's own page was unreachable or incomplete. One adversarial correction was made to the seed list: "ARES 70237" does not exist in ARES Tool's catalog (confirmed by direct site search and product-line browsing); it has been replaced with ARES 70214, the brand's actual 3/8 in. drive beam-type torque wrench and the nearest real product in the same 70XXX beam-wrench numbering series, included here specifically to give the roster a non-ratcheting beam mechanism example. Fields left null reflect specs genuinely not published by the source rather than estimates: several budget/import brands (Craftsman CMMT99433, Husky H2DTWA, Snap-on TECH2FR100, EPAuto, Neiko, ARES 70214) publish their torque scale in only one of ft-lb/in-lb/Nm and never state accuracy, tooth count, or weight on any fetched page. Snap-on's own shop.snapon.com is a JS-rendered dealer-locator page that returned no scrapeable content or public consumer pricing (Snap-on sells via mobile franchise dealers, not list price), so priceUsd is null there and a Snap-on-distributor mirror (snap-on.vn) plus secondary-market listings were used for specs/price context instead. TEKTON has discontinued the 24335 ("No Longer Available" on tekton.com); its entry is retained with a last-observed third-party price and a note that accuracy/length/weight were never published on the (now archival) manufacturer page. accessedAt 2026-08-09 throughout.

products.name: TEKTON 24335 1/2 in. Drive Click Torque Wrench (10-150 ft.-lb.)
products.priceNote: Last observed price at Techs Choice Tools & Equipment. TEKTON's own site marks the 24335 "No Longer Available" (discontinued) and its Amazon listing shows out of stock, so no current manufacturer MSRP exists.

specs.calibration_certificate: Not included — TEKTON's own product page states micrometer-style torque wrenches ship without a certificate of calibration; its split-beam line is recommended when certification is required

products.provenance: TEKTON's own product page (still live as an archival listing) confirms 1/2 in. drive, 10-150 ft-lb range, and micrometer click mechanism, and explicitly states no calibration certificate ships with this line. Accuracy, overall length, tooth count, and weight are not published anywhere on the page and the item is discontinued/out of stock at every retailer checked (Home Depot, Amazon, Walmart), so those fields are left null rather than inferred from TEKTON's other click-wrench models.

products.name: Precision Instruments PREC3FR250F 1/2 in. Drive Split-Beam Click Torque Wrench with Flex Head (40-250 ft-lb)
products.priceNote: List price on torqwrench.com, Precision Instruments' own direct-sale site. A NIST-traceable dated calibration certificate is a separate $20 add-on at checkout, not included in this base price.

specs.calibration_certificate: Optional add-on (+$20) for a dated, traceable certificate of calibration; standard unit ships with a 1-year warranty only

products.provenance: Precision Instruments' own e-commerce page (product code C3FR250F, sold under catalog number PREC3FR250F) confirms 1/2 in. drive, 40-250 ft-lb range in 5 ft-lb increments, 22-1/8 in. overall length (19 in. effective), 3.39 lb bare weight (4.33 lb with case), flex ratchet head, and Made in USA construction meeting GGG-W-686C/ANSI B107.14M. The page states accuracy only as "4%" without explicitly confirming direction; ±4% CW is the standard published rating for Precision Instruments' split-beam line and matches Amazon's reproduction of the spec sheet. Torque range in Nm is not published by Precision Instruments for this SAE-scale model, so torque_range_nm is left null rather than back-calculated.

specs.calibration_certificate: Included — ISO 6789 standards compliance with certificate of calibration

products.provenance: Retailer listings reproducing ACDelco's own spec sheet confirm 1/2 in. head, 14.8-147.5 ft-lb range, ±2%/±3% accuracy, LCD display in kg-cm/N-m/in-lb/ft-lb, buzzer + LED torque confirmation, AAA-battery power, hard-shell case, ISO 6789 compliance with calibration certificate, and 3.9 lb weight. products.name: Craftsman CMMT99433 3/8 in. Drive Micrometer Click Torque Wrench (20-100 ft-lb)
products.priceNote: Walmart current retail. Lowe's shows $56.98 with a MyLowe's Rewards member discount; Jackson's Hardware lists $129.99. $82.99 used as the price most consistently available without a membership requirement.

specs.calibration_certificate: Included — Craftsman.com states the wrench ships with a torque certification certificate

A retailer-aggregated weight figure of "12.96 lbs" appeared in one search result but is far outside the plausible range for a hand-held 3/8 in. torque wrench (likely a scraped shipping-carton or multipack weight); rather than propagate a figure that fails a basic sanity check, weight_lb is left null.

products.name: Park Tool TW-6.2 3/8 in. Drive Ratcheting Click-Type Torque Wrench (10-60 Nm)
products.priceNote: Current price at Worldwide Cyclery and other authorized Park Tool dealers (REI, Trisports); parktool.com itself shows the item temporarily out of stock without displaying a price.
products.provenance: Park Tool's own product page confirms 3/8 in. drive, 10-60 Nm range (88-530 in-lb) adjustable in 0.25 Nm increments, ±4% calibrated accuracy, 362mm (14.25 in.) overall length, bidirectional (CW/CCW) reading, and a 1-year warranty; a hard case is included. products.name: EPAuto 1/2-Inch Drive Click Torque Wrench with Extension Bar (10-150 ft-lb / 13.6-203.5 Nm)
products.priceNote: Lowest commonly-seen current price ("starts at just over $31" per one retailer listing); other listings cite a nominal price of ~$55 with frequent sale pricing around $38 (per an Autoblog deals article). Given no single stable manufacturer MSRP for this budget import SKU, $31.99 is used as the low-end verified figure and the wider $31-$55 range is noted here rather than picking an unverified midpoint.
products.provenance: EPAuto's retailer listings (Amazon, Walmart, and the reproduced spec copy on a third-party storefront) consistently describe a 1/2 in. drive click wrench, 10-150 ft-lb (13.6-203.5 Nm) dual-scale, hardened chrome-vanadium alloy ratchet head with corrosion-resistant satin finish, ±4% pre-calibration, a bundled 5 in. drive extension bar, a plastic storage case, and just-over-16-in. overall length (16.1 in. used as the closest stated figure). EPAuto does not publish a distinct model/catalog number beyond the retailer ASIN, no tooth count is stated, no calibration certificate is mentioned as included, and no net weight was found on any fetched source, so those fields are null. Walmart's product page returned only a bot-check/verification screen on direct fetch, so it is used here as a corroborating citation for the listing's existence and range rather than a source of additional spec detail.

products.name: ARES 70214 3/8 in. Drive Beam Torque Wrench (0-800 in-lb / 0-90 Nm)
products.priceNote: List price on arestool.com, the manufacturer's own direct-sale site.
products.provenance: CORRECTED FROM SEED: the seed model "ARES 70237" does not exist anywhere in ARES Tool's (MJD Industries) current or archived catalog — direct site search and browsing of both the beam-wrench (70XXX) and digital (43XXX) product lines on arestool.com turned up no such SKU. It was replaced with ARES 70214, a real current product in the same 70XXX beam-wrench numbering series and the only beam-mechanism entry in this roster (useful for the "mechanism" spec, since beam wrenches have no ratchet, click, or calibration-certificate mechanism to speak of by design). ARES's own page confirms 3/8 in. drive, 0-800 in-lb / 0-90 Nm range in 25 in-lb (11 Nm) increments, ±4% accuracy, high-visibility dual SAE/metric markings, and a no-wear/no-fatigue beam design under ARES's Performance Assurance warranty. torque_max_ft_lb (66.7) is a direct unit conversion of the published 800 in-lb figure (800 ÷ 12), not an estimate. No overall length, weight, or calibration-certificate statement is published, and tooth count is not applicable to a beam-type wrench (no ratchet gear), so those fields are null.
